lessons.name: Nyquist: a 44.1 kHz stream can represent frequencies up to HALF its rate — 44100 / 2 = 22050 Hz, the honest ceiling above which detail aliases. Not lossless, a bound.
lessons.why: Nyquist: a 44.1 kHz stream can represent frequencies up to HALF its rate — 44100 / 2 = 22050 Hz, the honest ceiling above which detail aliases. Not lossless, a bound.

lessons.name: An octave doubles frequency: A4 at 440 Hz is A5 at 880 — 440 · 2 = 880. The one interval every tuning agrees on.
lessons.why: An octave doubles frequency: A4 at 440 Hz is A5 at 880 — 440 · 2 = 880. The one interval every tuning agrees on.

lessons.name: The chromatic scale is the ring ℤ/12: twelve semitones, and the twelfth is the octave that wraps to the root — (List.range 12).length = 12 ∧ 12 % 12 = 0. Pitch counts in a ring, as the week does in ℤ/7.
lessons.why: The chromatic scale is the ring ℤ/12: twelve semitones, and the twelfth is the octave that wraps to the root — (List.range 12).length = 12 ∧ 12 % 12 = 0. Pitch counts in a ring, as the week does in ℤ/7.

lessons.name: Reversing a clip is self-inverse: reverse it twice and the signal returns — ([3,-5,8] : List Int).reverse.reverse = [3,-5,8]. The tape run backward and backward again is the tape.
lessons.why: Reversing a clip is self-inverse: reverse it twice and the signal returns — ([3,-5,8] : List Int).reverse.reverse = [3,-5,8]. The tape run backward and backward again is the tape.

lessons.name: Phase inversion is self-inverse: flip polarity (x ↦ −x) twice and the signal returns — (([3,-5,8] : List Int).map (−·)).map (−·) = [3,-5,8]. The polarity button, pressed twice, is off.

lessons.name: THE FUSION, the ultimate test: reverse-then-invert is ITSELF an involution — apply the fused operation twice and the signal returns, ((([3,-5,8] : List Int).reverse.map (−·)).reverse.map (−·)) = [3,-5,8]. Reverse and inverse compose to a clean self-inverse; the two studio mirrors fuse to one.

lessons.name: MIDI is 7-bit: 128 note numbers and 128 velocities, 0..127 — 2^7 = 128 ∧ 127 < 128. Why note 128 does not exist and velocity tops out at 127.
lessons.why: MIDI is 7-bit: 128 note numbers and 128 velocities, 0..127 — 2^7 = 128 ∧ 127 < 128. Why note 128 does not exist and velocity tops out at 127.

lessons.name: The rule of thumb: ~6 dB of dynamic range per bit, so 16-bit is ≈96 dB — 6 · 16 = 96. An approximation (the exact figure is ~6.02 dB/bit), the number an engineer reaches for.

lessons.name: At 120 BPM a beat is 500 ms and a 4/4 bar is 2000 ms: 60000 / 120 = 500 ∧ 4 · 500 = 2000 — the grid a DAW snaps every edit to.
lessons.why: At 120 BPM a beat is 500 ms and a 4/4 bar is 2000 ms: 60000 / 120 = 500 ∧ 4 · 500 = 2000 — the grid a DAW snaps every edit to.

lessons.name: The circle of fifths is ONE cycle: stepping by a perfect fifth (7 semitones) mod 12 visits all twelve tones, because 7 is coprime to 12 — every n in 0..11 appears in [(k·7) mod 12]. The pentagram {5/2} idea, heard in sound.
